hints: Notice the four different wordings: bounces back from a surface, passes into another medium, passes through an aperture, and are superposed.
Recall that diffraction is the spreading of a wave when it meets an obstacle edge or a narrow gap of width comparable to wavelength.
Compare each wording to reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference in turn to see which one describes spreading through a gap.
walkthrough: List what each option describes: A is bouncing back, B is changing medium, C is meeting a gap called an aperture, D is adding two waves together.

State the definitions: reflection is bouncing back, refraction is transmission into a new medium with change of speed, diffraction is spreading after passing an edge or aperture, interference is the superposition pattern.
Focus on option C: a wave passing through an aperture spreads into the region beyond the gap instead of continuing as a narrow beam.
Check the others do not fit: A fits reflection, B fits refraction, and D fits two-source interference by superposition.
Therefore the situation that defines diffraction is a wave passing through an aperture. This is option C.

options.A: A wave bouncing back from a surface is reflection, not the spreading at an edge or gap.
options.B: A wave passing from one medium into another and changing speed is refraction, not diffraction.
options.C: Passing through an aperture causes the wave to spread out, which is diffraction and is greatest when gap width is similar to wavelength.
options.D: Superposition of waves from two identical sources can produce interference, not diffraction by itself.
